title: Invoice Approval Workflow Template: 6 Options for 2026
summary: Invoice approval workflow templates send requests to approvers in their existing tools.
body_markdown:
## 6. Bill: best for dedicated accounts payable software


When you'd rather buy approvals, matching and payment as one product than build them, Bill is the pick.


Most teams aren't there yet:[CFO.com](https://www.cfo.com/news/for-mid-market-firms-full-ap-automation-is-a-long-way-off/813745/) reports that 89% of mid-market respondents automate only part of AP. Another 7% automate none and **just 4% automate fully** , so a purchased, end-to-end flow still closes a gap most peers have left open.


The cost gap shows what that partial state leaves on the table. The best-in-class team pays **$2.67 to process one invoice** , against an APQC median of $6.00 and an average of $9.90, so the average team pays about 3.7 times the best.


### How its built-in approval flow works


### Bill approval policies, matching and payment


Inside the product, you configure approval policies: invoices route to approvers by rules, matching checks them against purchase orders, and approved bills go straight to payment.


> The best-in-class team pays $2.67 to process one invoice, against an APQC median of $6.00 and an average of $9.90, so the average team pays about 3.7 times the best.


There's no separate trigger, extraction or logging step to assemble. Test your own routing rules in a trial before committing, since a policy that looks right in a demo can still misroute on your vendor data.


Bill charges per user, so the seat count, not invoice volume, drives the bill. Confirm in writing whether occasional approvers count as paid users. Check the current price list directly, because plans change.


### Bill audit trail and trade-offs


The audit trail and payment are the strong points. Every approval, edit and payment sits in one record, so an auditor's question about who approved an invoice has a single place to be answered.


Paying from the same system also removes the re-keying step where approved amounts drift from paid amounts.


Cost and flexibility are the trade-offs. Per-user billing grows with headcount, and the routing logic is whatever the policy screens allow. Buying beats building when your rules are ordinary and your priority is audit and payment, not custom logic.
